summary: The opening Q command reaches doquiver_core() after getobj() accepts inventory letter b. In this Ranger start, b is the alternate weapon (a bow), so C takes doquiver_core()'s uswapwep branch: with a singleton non-dual-wielded item it asks "That is your alternate weapon. Ready it instead?", then the recorded y answer clears uswapwep, sets the bow in uquiver, prints "b - a +1 bow (at the ready).", and returns ECMD_OK without random calls or time. JS implements only the inventory-empty, cancelled-prompt, and hands_obj arms, then throws at js/wield.js:680-682 for every ordinary item, so the fail-closed boundary stops at step 5. The later C steps confirm the state transition: t prompts, d supplies direction, and l throws an arrow by hand because the bow is now quivered. The source-faithful fix belongs to wield.c doquiver_core(); it must preserve the alternate-weapon confirmation, slot changes, inventory print, result bits, and the separate fire caller. Generalizing beyond this witness also needs a shared ynq path and pair_of() semantics; neither should be inferred from the witness's singleton bow.
